facts.claim: Neither the RP nor the LRP index neural processes are causal of conscious willing.
facts.quote: neither the RP nor the LRP index neural processes are causal of conscious willing.

facts.claim: Both the RP and the LRP seem unrelated to conscious intentions to move.
facts.quote: Both potentials seem unrelated to conscious intentions to move.

facts.claim: The link between the Libet paradigm and free will or moral responsibility is not clear.
facts.quote: While the Libet paradigm may be useful for examining how stimuli affect temporal judgments, the link between this and free will or moral responsibility is not clear.

facts.claim: The readiness potential (RP) is a slow buildup of electrical potential recorded at the scalp using electroencephalography that is associated with neural activity involved in movement preparation.
facts.quote: The readiness potential (RP), a slow buildup of electrical potential recorded at the scalp using electroencephalography, has been associated with neural activity involved in movement preparation.

facts.claim: The readiness potential (RP) precedes the reported time of decision to act by a few hundred milliseconds.
facts.quote: cognitive neuroscientists such as Benjamin Libet have joined the discussion by demonstrating that an ERP component, the readiness potential (RP), precedes the reported time of decision to act by a few hundred milliseconds.

rejected.claim: The lateralized readiness potential (LRP) likely reflects uniquely motor-related processing.
rejected.quote: the readiness potential (RP) does not reflect uniquely motor-related processing, while the lateralized readiness potential (LRP) likely does
rejected.reason: quote not found in the source

research.angle: While the readiness potential precedes reported decisions, research suggests it is not causal of conscious willing and its link to free will remains unclear.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that the readiness potential is associated with movement preparation but is not a causal driver of conscious intention.
research.caveat: The exact nature of the neural processes involved in these potentials remains unclear.
